content_voiceover: This table outlines the risk classification for the TPOG-Infant ALL-2022 protocol, which is specifically for infants with acute lymphoblastic leukemia, stratified by KMT2A gene status. First, if KMT2A is germline, meaning no rearrangement, the patient is low risk and is treated on the standard TPOG-ALL-2021 protocol, provisionally as high risk. Second, if KMT2A is rearranged but there are no high risk clinical features, the patient is intermediate risk. Within that group, if MRD is less than 0.01 percent after consolidation, at the time point called TP4, the patient stays on the intermediate risk infant protocol. If MRD remains higher than that, the patient is escalated to intermediate risk plus either transplant or CAR-T cell therapy. Third, if KMT2A is rearranged and high risk clinical features are present, meaning age less than six months, or a white blood cell count of 300,000 per cubic millimeter or higher, the patient is classified as high risk. Again, if MRD is less than 0.01 percent after consolidation at TP4, they follow the high risk infant protocol alone, but if MRD remains elevated, they escalate to high risk plus transplant or CAR-T. So the take home is that infant ALL risk stratification depends on both the genetic driver, KMT2A rearrangement status, clinical high risk features like young age and hyperleukocytosis, and early treatment response measured by MRD.
keypoints: KMT2A germline infant ALL is low risk, treated on standard TPOG-ALL-2021 protocol
KMT2A rearranged without high-risk features is intermediate risk
High-risk features are age under six months or WBC 300,000 per mm3 or higher
MRD under 0.01 percent after consolidation, TP4, keeps patients on IR or HR protocol alone
Persistent MRD at TP4 escalates either group to HSCT or CAR-T therapy
keypoint_voiceover: Quick recap. KMT2A germline infants are low risk and follow the standard ALL protocol. KMT2A rearranged infants without high-risk features are intermediate risk, while age under six months or WBC over 300,000 defines high risk. In both intermediate and high risk groups, MRD less than 0.01 percent after consolidation at TP4 means staying on that risk-adapted protocol, but persistent MRD escalates the patient to transplant or CAR-T therapy.
